page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top, printed page number at the top right. No margin notes. Below the text: a signature at the lower left and a catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: caeteros uel negligimus, ut indignos nostra beneuolentia[?]: uel odio habemus, le-uicula ἀφοφμὴ[?] irritati. Nota est pijs omnibus ingenua Dauidis confessio: Ego uero dicebam in prosperitate mea: Non mouebor in æternum. Iehouah, tu pro beneplacito tuo stabiliueras monti meo robur. Psal.3o.6.7. Verùm de hac parte ista dixisse satis esto.

Vbi uero inopinatę ruinæ se proximos, aut etiam se iam cocidisse uident, cum Salomone exclamant: Vanitas uanitatū, & omnia uanitas. Ecclesiast.1.1. Hanc sententiam ferunt clara uoce recitauisse Vandalorum Regem Gilimerum, cum à Belisario acie uictus & captus, Constantinopolim in triumpho ductus, & ad pedes Iustiniani Imperatoris prostratus iaceret, anno Christi 534.
Quomodo hoc rerum statu ægerani-mus, dum sibi relinquitur, semper pauidus & attonitus erret in consilijs & conatibus suis, hæc sequentia docent.
Rectè quidem homo in aduersis, veluti cuiusdam labyrinthi tricis, hærens, de liberatione sibi consultandum & follici-

page.notes: The Greek word after "habemus, le-uicula" is hard to read and is marked [?]. "beneuolentia" is uncertain (the letters may be "beneeuolentia") and is marked [?]. The numerals "3o" in "Psal.3o.6.7." are read as printed and may be "30". The catchword "tè labo-" sits at the right below the last full line, with the signature "c 4" at the left.
